title: Remote CLI mailbox read via relay intermittently returns 423 'authenticated native mailbox relay refused'; a stale-receipt ack is then accepted
outcome: A satellite CLI mailbox read through the native relay either succeeds or returns a specific, actionable reason. The generic 'refused; check original identity, home and request' message, which hides the home's actual 4xx reason, no longer appears. Acknowledging with a receipt from an earlier, already processed page has a defined, documented result.
acceptance: Record a code-only diagnosis of the native relay page-read paths that can return HTTP 423, separating the reported DL560 incident from source-inferred causes. No new live probe or other sessions' mailbox read is used; the incident's exact home refusal remains unknown unless existing evidence identifies it.

An authenticated native mailbox relay refusal preserves the original HTTP status and exposes only a closed, bounded home reason code with safe actionable guidance. Known home persistence-settling refusals are distinguished from identity or receipt failures. Unknown, malformed, oversized or unsupported reason data fails closed with a reason-unavailable fallback; raw home error text, message bodies and sensitive identity/store data are never forwarded. Authentication, identity, membership, authority, request and outcome-uncertainty gates remain unchanged, with behavioral positive and negative tests.

Document and test the existing native receipt rule: an issued receipt remains bound to its original participant and mailbox; a later read does not revoke it. Re-acknowledging a valid older receipt at or behind the current cursor succeeds idempotently without moving the cursor backward, acknowledging newer unread messages, issuing a new receipt or suppressing their owed wake. Foreign or unissued receipts and acknowledgements that skip unprocessed visible messages remain refused.

Record passing registered focused coverage on the final source, an independent Codex/Claude review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding, and a passing full five-stage gate on the exact final committed input before landing.
